text:
A: Hello! Hi, can you hear me?
B: Yeah, hiya. I'm Rob.
A: Marites. Nice to meet you. Sorry, my phone, it's leaning on the rice cooker.
B: That's fine. Whatever works.
A: Hehe. Erm, I saw your picture, you have the binoculars and the birds. Are you a student?
B: Yeah, good guess. Ecology, at Man Met in Manchester. Second year. I'm thirty-one, though, so a bit of a late one.
A: Oh, that's good! That's never too late. What did you do before?
B: Admin at a council. Eight years. I got bored, so I packed it in and went back to uni.
A: Wow. That's brave. My cousin keeps telling me, Marites, you should do the nursing associate training. And I say, maybe when Rafael is older. Every time, maybe when Rafael is older.
B: What do you do now, then?
A: I'm a carer. Home care in Croydon. I visit old people, help them wash, dress, give them breakfast, check the medicine.
B: That's proper work, that. My nan had carers at the end, and they were brilliant with her. I don't know how they did it, to be honest.
A: Oh, thank you. Yeah, sometimes it's hard. But I like them. Most of them, hehe.
B: Ha. Most of them. Fair enough.
A: And the nursing, I think maybe I'm too old, and the studying, the online modules, I'm not good. At work they have the online training and I only just finish them.
B: Honestly, I thought that too. I'd dropped out at eighteen, so I was dreading it. But I did an Access course first, part-time, and that sort of eased me back in. Half my course are nineteen, but there's a few of us older ones. You wouldn't be the only one.
A: Really? That's good to know. Maybe. I don't know.
B: No pressure. Just saying it's doable.
A: Thank you. Erm, do you have birds in Manchester? Sorry, that's a silly question, of course you have birds.
B: Ha, not silly. Loads, yeah. You've got parakeets where you are, haven't you? Down in South London.
A: The green ones! Yes! They're so loud. In the morning, near the park, screaming. I thought they escaped from somebody's house.
B: That's sort of the story, yeah. Nobody really knows how they started, but there's thousands of them now. Ring-necked parakeets. I'd love to see a big flock, actually. We don't really get them up north.
A: You can come to Croydon, I will show you, hehe. Very easy to find, just listen.
B: I might take you up on that.
A: Do you have children?
B: No. Just a cat. Moss. She's a rescue. She mostly knocks things off my desk.
A: Oh, my plants are like that, but they don't knock things, they just die because I forget to water.
B: Moss would eat them anyway.
A: Hehe. Do you cook, or your partner cooks?
B: I do most of the tea in the week, 'cause my timetable's looser. Curries, chilli, one-pot stuff. Bit less meat these days.
A: Tea? You mean dinner?
B: Yeah, sorry. Tea's dinner up here. The evening meal.
